bundled icon (`src/chatimport/assets/icon.png`, `icon.ico`).

# Project: ChatImport

ChatImport is a background service that keeps a full local text archive of the Telegram
groups and channels listed in the owner's `chats.toml` library. It runs as its own session
of the owner's account (Telethon, MTProto), backfills each chat's history once, then appends
new messages in small batches (every 5 messages or 30 seconds), rechecks the last 7 days
daily for edits and deletions, and protects free disk space by trimming the oldest parts.
Output is JSONL in a `ChatImport` folder (the Desktop by default). Product intent:
`docs/vision.md`; design: `docs/architecture.md`.

This is branch `chatimport`, a parallel line to ChatRadar on `main`. The two are meant to
become one product later (`docs/architecture.md` §15): ChatImport's JSONL folder is a
candidate raw store for ChatRadar.

**Stage: 0.1-0.7 implemented and hardened (2026-10-30); the owner's live check with a real
account is next, then 1.0 (ChatRadar integration).**

## Repository map

Single uv project on Python 3.14+ (`src/` layout, package `chatimport`). `src/chatimport/`:

- **Core:** `config` (TOML to dataclasses), `config_edit` (writes `output.root_dir`),
  `toml_edit` (comment-keeping line edits), `paths` (app folders, data root, OneDrive check),
  `records` (record types, JSONL lines), `ports` (gateway, clock, disk protocols, errors),
  `runtime` (chat handles, registry, notifier, `BackfillSlots`), `textnorm` (`fold`,
  `transliterate`), `refs` (the one ref parser), `logging_setup` (rotating file log).
- **Library:** `library` (`chats.toml` parse, diff, watch, add/enable), `resolution` (entries
  to chats, error book), `offline` (CLI work without the service: trim, floor, selector).
- **Service:** `app` (facade: run, run --once, library loop, set-root), `context` (config,
  folders, gateway), `service_runtime` (everything on one data root), `supervisor`
  (restarts with backoff), `router` (events to workers, `_unrouted_deletes.jsonl`),
  `commands` (command registry), `control` (control folder, instance lock), `status`
  (`_status.json`), `recheck` (daily comparison and scheduler).
- **Worker:** `worker` (`ChatWorker` facade), `worker_signals` (flags), `worker_live` and
  `worker_buffer` (live intake), `worker_backfill` (head and tail), `worker_store` (folder
  access, threads), `flood` (FloodWait).
- **Maintenance:** `trim`, `media` (downloader), `integrity` (`check`), `export`
  (`export-json`), `setroot`, `guards/disk` (disk guard, media gate), `guards/folders`.
- **Storage:** `layout`, `state`, `writer`, `reader`, `recover`, `fileio` (atomic and
  retried file primitives), `chat_store` (one chat folder), `month_commit` (journalled
  month rewrite), `media_files` (media names, safe extensions).
- **Telegram (only Telethon user):** `client` (gateway, login), `resolve`, `mapper` (pure).
- **Interfaces:** `cli` (entry point) with `cli_support`, `cli_chats`, `cli_service`,
  `cli_data`; `tray` with `tray_dialogs`; `__main__`.

Elsewhere:

- `config.example.toml`, `chats.example.toml` — templates; the real files live in the
  application data folder and are never tracked.
- `tests/unit/<area>`, `tests/integration`, `tests/fakes.py` (clock, disk, scripted gateway);
  `tests/fixtures/` is reserved for anonymized data and does not exist yet.
- `scripts/` — stdlib-only repo tooling: `sync_agents.py`, `check_language.py`, `doctor.py`.
- `justfile`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.github/`.
- `docs/` — `vision.md`, `architecture.md` (§12 lists every module), `ROADMAP.md`,
  `decisions.md`, `backlog.md`, `adr/`.
- `.ai/`, `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md` — assistant rules.

## Language policy

- **Everything tracked by git is English**: code, comments, docstrings, CLI help, docs, rule
  modules, commit messages, test names, `task-checklist.md`. Owner decision 2026-10-19.
- `python scripts/check_language.py` fails on any Cyrillic character in a tracked file,
  except under `tests/fixtures/` (anonymized chat data is Russian by nature).
- The owner's original spec is Russian and lives outside the repository;
  `docs/architecture.md` is its English version and the reference inside the repository.
- Reports to the owner in chat are in Russian, short and step by step.

## Documentation policy

- `docs/vision.md` changes only when the product intent changes, by owner agreement.
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` is the plan and progress record; `docs/decisions.md` the decision log.
- The no-new-docs exception (`03-scope-and-code-style.md`) covers `README.md`, `docs/` and
  `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Product guardrails

- Only chats listed and enabled in `chats.toml` are read or stored; private dialogs, bots
  and everything else are dropped at the router.
- The service never joins a chat by itself and never sends anything to Telegram.
- Data stays on the owner's disk. Sender names are personal data (Uruguay, Ley 18.331):
  any export or publication strips them.
- Telegram is read through the owner's user account with pauses and FloodWait respected;
  history backfill runs one chat at a time.
- **Stage order in `docs/ROADMAP.md` is binding.** Skipping ahead needs an owner decision
  recorded in `docs/decisions.md`.

# Project Commands and Quality Gates

All commands run from the repository root (PowerShell or Git Bash on Windows, any POSIX
shell elsewhere). Toolchain: uv (it installs Python 3.14 from `.python-version`), git,
just; `python scripts/doctor.py` checks all of them read-only.

## The one gate

```bash
just check        # lint, format, pyright strict, pytest, agents sync, language
```

CI runs the same sections as separate jobs. Without `just`, run the recipe's lines from
`justfile` one by one through `uv run`.

| Recipe | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `setup` | `uv sync` + install the pre-commit hook, once per clone |
| `fmt` / `lint` | ruff format + fix / ruff check and format check |
| `typecheck` | pyright strict over `src/`, `tests/`, `scripts/` |
| `test` / `cov` | pytest / with coverage |
| `agents` / `agents-check` | regenerate / verify `AGENTS.md` and `.codex/` |
| `language` | no Cyrillic outside the allowed data paths |
| `doctor` | read-only toolchain check |
| `hooks` | every pre-commit hook over the whole repository |

**Standing duty — keep the tooling true.** A task that changes how the project is checked,
built, run or published updates `justfile`, the CI workflow and this table in the same
task. A source whose artifact is generated (`AGENTS.md`, `.codex/agents|skills`) is
committed together with the regenerated artifact.

## Main branch (strict, owner instruction 2026-10-29)

**In this repository `chatimport` IS the main branch.** Everywhere a rule, skill, agent or
habit says `main`, read `chatimport`: branch from it, merge into it, compare against it,
push it. Never check out, modify, merge into, rebase onto or push `main` — it holds the
unrelated ChatRadar project and is off limits. If a command or document names `main`,
substitute `chatimport` and do not ask.

## Publishing

- No pull requests (owner workflow shared with the owner's other repositories).
- **This line of work lives on branch `chatimport`, not `main`.** Task branches start from
  `chatimport` (`type/short-description`) and merge back into it with
  `git merge --ff-only` after a green `just check`; then `git push origin chatimport`.
  `main` (ChatRadar) is never touched from this branch; joining the two is a separate
  owner decision.
- Agents push only when the owner asked for it in the current task. Never force-push.

## Gate policy

- `just check` is green before any merge into `chatimport`. Docs- and config-only changes
  still run it: the agents-sync and language sections cover them.
- The pre-commit hook formats and checks hygiene, secrets, pyright and generated files;
  it never replaces the full gate.
- Never skip a hook (`--no-verify`) or weaken a check to get green.

# Domain Rules and House Style (ChatImport)

These sharpen the universal rules for this codebase. Stricter wins.

## Python code

- Python 3.14+, full type hints, pyright strict is a gate. A `# type: ignore` or
  `# pyright: ignore` names its rule; a `# noqa` names its code and says why.
- Ruff rules in `pyproject.toml` are binding; `T20` bans `print`, `DTZ` bans naive datetimes.
- A module past roughly 500 lines is split by meaning. `cli*.py` and `tray*.py` hold
  argument parsing, menus and wiring only.
- Dependencies only through `uv add` / `uv add --dev`; `uv.lock` is committed. Only free
  open-source dependencies; a new one is added with the code that first uses it.

## Boundaries

- `telegram/mapper.py`, the storage layout and `trim` are pure or file-only: no Telethon
  client, no tray, no CLI imports. This keeps them portable into ChatRadar later.
- Telethon is touched only in `telegram/`. Everything else receives plain records.
- Collaborators come in through constructors (Telegram client, `disk_usage`, clock), so
  every component is testable without network and without a real disk.

## Data rules

- **One writer.** Only the service process writes into the `ChatImport` folder, and inside
  it only the chat's worker (or the trimmer holding that chat's lock). CLI and tray send
  commands through the control folder; the service claims each command file by renaming it
  and runs it at most once. Without a running service the CLI takes the instance lock and
  is that one writer.
- Records are JSONL, one object per line, schema field `v`. Adding a field keeps `v`;
  removing or changing meaning bumps it. History is append-only: edits and deletions are
  new `edit`/`delete` records, never rewrites.
- Files are `YYYY-MM_NNN.jsonl` (UTC month, part number); a part is the unit of storage,
  accounting and trimming. Lines inside a part ascend by `msg_id`.
- At-least-once intake plus deduplication by `msg_id` (`last_id` in `state.json`): no
  duplicates and no gaps after a crash or restart.
- `state.json` is a cache; the JSONL files are the truth. It is written atomically
  (temp file, `fsync`, `os.replace`) and rebuilt from the files when missing or broken,
  never when it exists but cannot be read now (`StateUnreadable`). A month of several parts
  is rewritten only through the journal in `storage/month_commit.py`.
- Data files are never held open between writes (Windows must be able to delete a folder).
- Trimming removes oldest first, never selectively, and raises `floor_id`; the service
  never backfills below `floor_id` on its own.
- All datetimes are timezone-aware UTC, written as ISO 8601 with `Z`.

## Telegram and privacy

- A `*.session` file is full access to an account: it lives in the application data folder,
  is never read into a transcript, logged, committed or copied.
- `api_id`/`api_hash` live only in the real `config.toml`; the repository holds
  `config.example.toml`.
- Respect FloodWait, pause between requests and chats, backfill one chat at a time
  (`runtime.BackfillSlots`, `backfill.max_parallel_chats = 1`); do not shorten pauses.
- Logs carry chat ids, message ids and counts, never message text, sender names or invite
  hashes.

## Tests

- Telegram is never called in tests: a scripted gateway (`tests/fakes.py`) replays history
  and events.
- Unit tests need no network and touch only `tmp_path`: the autouse fixture in
  `tests/conftest.py` isolates `CHATIMPORT_*` variables and the working directory.
- Mapper, chunking, recover and trim are table-driven; size thresholds are shrunk in tests
  (for example 1 KB parts) instead of writing large files.
- Fixtures in `tests/fixtures/` are anonymized: no real names, usernames or phone numbers.
  Real exports may be studied only locally and only as aggregates.

## Assistant workspaces

- `.claude/agents` and `.claude/skills` are the source; `.codex/agents|skills` are generated
  from them by `just agents`. Never edit `.codex/agents|skills` or `AGENTS.md` by hand.
- `.claude/settings.json` allowlists routine read and verification commands and denies
  destructive git operations and reading secrets. Extend the allowlist rather than routing
  around it; never remove a deny entry without owner approval.

# Project Progress Tracking

Purpose: any assistant, in any session, on any model, can locate exactly where the project
stands and where it is going — **from files, not from memory**. This is the primary
recovery mechanism after a lost conversation.

## Where the truth lives

| Question | File |
|---|---|
| What the product should become | `docs/vision.md` |
| How it is designed, step by step | `docs/architecture.md` |
| What is planned, in what order, what is done | `docs/ROADMAP.md` |
| Owner decisions and open questions | `docs/decisions.md` |
| Work consciously deferred, to come back to | `docs/backlog.md` |
| Significant architecture decisions | `docs/adr/` |
| What the current or last task was | `task-checklist.md` |
| What actually happened recently | `git log -15 --date=iso-strict --pretty=format:"%h %cd %s"` |
| How the rules themselves changed | `.ai/CHANGELOG.md` |
| What users can see changed | `CHANGELOG.md` |

## Orientation ritual — at the start of EVERY task

1. `git status --short --branch` and
   `git log -15 --date=iso-strict --pretty=format:"%h %cd %s"`.
2. `docs/ROADMAP.md` — **the first step without a `**Status.**` line is next**, unless the
   owner says otherwise.
3. `task-checklist.md` — what the previous task was and whether it finished cleanly.
4. `docs/decisions.md` — whether a decision changes the plan.
5. `docs/architecture.md` — the section for the step you are about to implement.
6. Only then plan the new task.

## Update duties when finishing work

- Finished a roadmap step or a significant slice → add or refresh its `**Status.**` line in
  `docs/ROADMAP.md` (date, what shipped) and the status column of the table.
- Changed the system's shape (a module, table, command, stage, setting) → update
  `.ai/project/10-project-map.md` and, if the design moved, `docs/architecture.md`.
- Owner decision that constrains future work → `docs/decisions.md`, not only the chat.
- Work you chose not to do or could not finish → `docs/backlog.md`, with the reason; never
  only the chat. Shipped items move to `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Significant architecture decision → a new ADR in `docs/adr/`.
- Changed a rule module, agent or skill → `.ai/CHANGELOG.md` and `just agents`.
- Changed what a user installs, configures or sees → `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Drift guard

If the plan, the state documents and the code disagree: **the code is the fact, the plan is
the intent**. Reconcile them in the same task or report the mismatch explicitly. Stale
documentation is worse than no documentation.

## Unfinished-task rule

If `task-checklist.md` still holds open `[ ]` items from a previous session, resolve them
first: finish them, or mark them `-` with an honest note.

# Command Reference and Platform Notes

<!-- tier: extended -->

> **Essence.** Lookup material — every `chatimport` command (all implemented) and whether it needs the running service, where configuration, data and logs live, the control-queue protocol (claimed by rename, run at most once), CI jobs (pyright on Linux) and the Windows notes (UTF-8 consoles, `pythonw` autostart, files closed between writes, `os.replace` within one volume); the always-apply policies live in `11-commands.md`.

## CLI (`chatimport`)

Every command of the spec (`docs/architecture.md` §9) is implemented (`cli.py` plus
`cli_chats.py`, `cli_service.py`, `cli_data.py`). Global options: `--version`, `--root <path>`
(output folder for this run). "Service" says what happens when the service is running.

| Command | What it does | Service |
|---|---|---|
| `login` | first login: phone, code, 2FA password; creates the session | refused (needs the instance lock) |
| `dialogs` | the account's groups and channels with `chat_id`, kind, title, link | refused |
| `chats list` | every library entry, its resolution and stored record count | refused |
| `chats add <ref> [--name N]` / `chats disable\|enable <name or ref>` | edit `chats.toml` | not needed; the service rereads the file |
| `run [--once] [--chat X]` | console mode, logs to console and file; `--once` backfills or catches up every chat (or one) and exits, continuing past a failing chat | refused (one instance) |
| `tray` | normal mode with a tray icon, logs to file | refused |
| `status` | service state, disk, per-chat phase, `last_id`, records | asks the service; otherwise prints the last `_status.json` as stopped |
| `pause` / `resume [--chat X]` | stop and continue collecting; a pause survives a restart | required |
| `recheck [--chat X] [--days N]` | compare recent days with Telegram now | required |
| `trim {25,50,75} [--chat X] [--yes]` | delete the oldest share of each chat's history; asks `y/N` | sent to the service; else runs offline |
| `backfill --deeper [--chat X]` | lower `floor_id` so older history is fetched | sent; else lowers the floor offline |
| `check [--repair]` | integrity of parts, `state.json`, saved media and leftover temp files; `--repair` runs recover | sent; else runs offline |
| `export-json --chat X [--out F] [--names\|--no-names]` | one JSON array; default `<root>/_exports/<chat folder>.json`, sender names and `raw` left out unless `--names` | reads files directly |
| `set-root <path> [--move] [--yes]` | change the output folder; without `--move` asks, then chats are refetched | sent; else moves offline |

`--chat` accepts a library name, `@username`, link, numeric id, folder name or title; text is
compared through `textnorm.fold` (NFC, casefold). Exit codes: 1 error, 2 not configured.
The control registry also has `reload_config`, `shutdown` and `refetch` (tray and service
only).

## Where things live

Resolved through `platformdirs`. Windows paths shown:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Chat data | `<Desktop>\ChatImport\` (override: `--root`, `CHATIMPORT_ROOT`, `output.root_dir`) |
| Service files in the data root | `_status.json`, `_trim_log.jsonl`, `_unrouted_deletes.jsonl` (capped at 2 MiB), `_exports\` |
| Config, library | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ChatImport\config.toml`, `chats.toml` |
| Session | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ChatImport\session\chatimport.session` |
| Log | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ChatImport\logs\chatimport.log` (UTF-8, rotating 5 MiB x 5) |
| Icon | `src/chatimport/assets/icon.png` and `icon.ico` (`chatimport.assets`); the tray draws the PNG with a state badge |
| Lock, control queue | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ChatImport\chatimport.lock`, `control\` |

`run`, `status` and the tray warn when the data root is under OneDrive; `set-root` refuses
the application folder (it holds the session).

## Control queue

The CLI writes `<command>-<uuid>.json` atomically into `control\` and waits for
`<command>-<uuid>.result.json`. The service polls every second, claims a file by renaming it
to `.<command>-<uuid>.claimed` and only then runs it, so a command runs **at most once**; a
claim left by a crash is answered "interrupted", never re-run. Files over 64 KiB or not a
JSON object are rejected. The CLI waits 30 s, 10 min for `trim`, `check`, `deeper` and
`recheck`, 1 h for `set_root`; on a timeout after the claim it says not to repeat the command.

## CI (`.github/workflows/`)

- `ci.yml` (pushes to `main` and `chatimport`): lint (uv lock check, ruff), typecheck,
  tests on Ubuntu and Windows with Python 3.14, assistants sync and language check,
  gitleaks.
- **pyright runs on Linux in CI.** Windows-only code must sit behind a `sys.platform ==
  "win32"` check that pyright understands, or it is reported as unreachable or untyped there.
- `codeql.yml`: Python and Actions, weekly and on `main`/`chatimport`.
- Dependabot only reads the default branch (`main`); updates for this branch are manual.

## Windows notes

- Console output: the `chatimport` entry point (`cli.run`) reconfigures stdout and stderr
  to UTF-8 unless `PYTHONIOENCODING` is set, otherwise Rich help crashes on cp1252 pipes.
  Call `run`, not `app`, from scripts.
- Autostart: Task Scheduler at logon with a 1-minute delay, running
  `.venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe -m chatimport tray` (no console window).
- Close every data file after each write, or Explorer cannot delete the chat folder.
- `os.replace` is atomic only within one volume: write temp files next to the target.
  A reader holding a file (antivirus, indexer) makes `os.replace`/`unlink` fail briefly;
  `storage/fileio.py` retries them.
- Auto-trimming deletes with `os.remove`, never to the Recycle Bin, or no space is freed.
- Downloaded media get a `Zone.Identifier` stream (Mark-of-the-Web).
- If the Desktop syncs to OneDrive, set `output.root_dir` outside it.
- Prefer `uv run <tool>` over the `.venv/Scripts/*.exe` shims.

# AI Assistant Rule Modules

Single source of truth for the rules that govern every AI assistant (Claude Code first,
Codex, Gemini CLI and any future agent) working in this repository.

## How it works

```text
.ai/universal/*.md   Portable rules, valid for ANY project. No project names, paths or
                     stack specifics.
.ai/project/*.md     Rules for THIS project: map, commands, domain rules, progress
                     tracking, command reference.
CLAUDE.md            Claude Code entry point; imports every module with native @path syntax.
AGENTS.md            Codex (and any AGENTS.md reader) entry point. GENERATED by
                     concatenating the same modules. Never edit by hand.
GEMINI.md            Gemini CLI entry point; imports AGENTS.md.
.claude/agents|skills  Project subagents and skills — the source.
.codex/agents|skills   GENERATED mirror of .claude/agents|skills.
.ai/CHANGELOG.md     History of rule changes: what, why, when, who decided.
```

Modules load in filename order: `universal/01..NN` first, then `project/10..NN`. Project
rules win over universal rules when they conflict.

## Editing rules

1. Edit or add a module under `.ai/universal/` or `.ai/project/` (or an agent or skill
   under `.claude/`).
2. Record the change in `.ai/CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Regenerate: `just agents` (`uv run python scripts/sync_agents.py`) — writes `AGENTS.md`
   and `.codex/agents|skills`.
4. Commit the source, the changelog entry and the regenerated files together.

`just check`, the pre-commit hook and CI fail while anything generated is out of date.
`CLAUDE.md` needs no regeneration: Claude Code resolves `@` imports at session start.

The protocol for changing rules — when it is allowed, who decides — is
`universal/08-rules-evolution.md`. Read it before touching a module.

## Size budget and module tiers

Codex reads at most 32 KiB of project instructions; `sync_agents.py` fails above 30 KiB.

- **inline** (default) — embedded in `AGENTS.md` in full.
- **extended** — only the title, path and essence are embedded. Opt in with
  `<!-- tier: extended -->` in the first five lines, and put
  `> **Essence.** One sentence covering the module's core rules.` right after the title.

Extended modules bind exactly like inline ones. `CLAUDE.md` imports every module
regardless of tier.

## Origin

The universal modules and this layout come from the owner's `daily-quest`, `codepack` and
`CogniBoiler` repositories (identical `universal/` content); adapted on 2026-10-19.

# Workflow: Git, Branches, Commits

Purpose: every task follows one predictable git cycle. No exceptions without an
explicit owner instruction in the current conversation.

## Branch discipline

- NEVER develop directly on `main`.
- Start every task from up-to-date `main`:
  `git checkout main` → `git pull --ff-only origin main` → `git checkout -b <branch>`.
- Branch name format: `type/short-task-description`
  (types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, `docs`, `ci`, `perf`, `security`).
- Uninformative branch names (`test`, `fix`, `work`, `final`, `new`) are forbidden.
- Merge into `main` only fast-forward (`git merge --ff-only`) and only after the
  project's full quality gate is green.
- Push to `origin/main` only when the owner explicitly asked for a publish within the
  current task. Work-in-progress branch pushes are allowed (for example, to publish
  the task checklist before starting work).
- Delete the task branch after it is merged.

## Commits

- Message format: `type: short description of what and why`.
- One commit = one logically complete unit. Do not mix a bug fix, a refactor,
  formatting, and new features in a single commit unless they are one inseparable task.
- Forbidden messages: `fix`, `update`, `wip`, `changes`, `final`, `123`.
- Keep commits attributable: include the assistant identity trailer the project already
  uses (check a recent `git log` for the convention).

## Quality gate before merge

- Run the project's checks (see the project commands module) before merging.
- If mandatory checks fail, merging into `main` is forbidden until fixed or the owner
  explicitly decides otherwise.
- Before merging, self-review the diff: changes match the task, no stray files, no
  debug leftovers, no secrets, no accidental unrelated edits.

When unsure whether an action counts as "explicitly requested": ask, or stop after the
branch commit and report instead of pushing.

# Task Checklist and Definition of Done

Purpose: every task is planned before it starts and honestly accounted for after it
ends, in a file any reviewer can read without the conversation.

## task-checklist.md protocol

A file named `task-checklist.md` lives in the repository root and is always tracked by
git (never in `.gitignore`).

Before starting a task:

1. Clear or recreate `task-checklist.md` for the new task.
2. Write the main stages, checks, and expected outcomes as `[ ]` items, grouped into
   short sections (preparation / implementation / verification / completion).
   Moderate detail — stages, not keystrokes.
3. Commit the checklist BEFORE doing the main work.

After finishing the task:

4. Mark every item: `+` done, `-` not done or partially done.
5. Commit the filled checklist together with the completed work.
6. Never hide unfinished items — a `-` with an honest note is correct; a silently
   ignored item is a violation.

## Definition of Done

A task is complete only when ALL of the following hold:

- code written and matching the task, without unrequested scope;
- code formatted; lint and type checks pass;
- tests added or updated where reasonable; existing tests pass;
- project builds; no obvious errors in logs;
- no secrets, no temp files, no accidental changes in unrelated files;
- architecture and state docs updated if the task changed the system's shape;
- task checklist filled with `+`/`-`;
- final report written.

## Final report

The final report is ALWAYS the last step of a task. It states: what was done; which
files and areas changed; which checks ran and their results; dependency, API, database,
or config changes; security, performance, and compatibility risks; and — explicitly and
honestly — anything that was not done or failed.

# Scope Control and Code Style

Purpose: change only what the task requires, and keep code readable without decoration.

## Minimal changes

- Touch only what the current task needs. Forbidden without necessity:
  mass-reformatting other files, renaming things outside the task, changing
  architecture "while at it", rewriting working code without cause, changing UI when
  the task is not about the interface, deleting existing functionality without a
  direct requirement.
- If you discover an unrelated problem, record it separately (report it, or file it per
  the project's process) — do not mix it into the current diff.
- Do not create new documentation (README, `.md`, `.txt`) unless the task requires it
  directly. Exception: the project's designated architecture and progress documents,
  which must be kept current.

## Comments

- No comments by default. Code must be clear through structure and naming.
- A comment is allowed only when the task demands it, or when important logic stays
  non-obvious even with good naming. It explains the non-obvious "why", never restates
  the code.
- Stale, false, or misleading comments are forbidden. No doc comments that merely
  repeat a function name.

## File size

- Regular code files: keep under roughly 1000 lines; split by meaning when approaching
  the limit. Projects may set a stricter limit — the stricter limit wins.
- Application entry points (`main`-type files): under roughly 100 lines; extract
  configuration, startup, and service initialization into modules.
- Exemptions: test files, developer-tool scripts, and any files the project explicitly
  exempts.

## Frontend restraint

- No visual polish (styling, animations, decorative elements, redesign) unless the task
  is explicitly about appearance.
- When a task needs an interface, build the minimum that exercises the business logic
  correctly.
- Never change visual style, interface structure, component behavior, or user flows
  without a direct requirement.

# Architecture Boundaries, Workarounds, Tech Debt

Purpose: respect the project's layering; make every shortcut visible.

## Boundaries

- Follow the project's existing architecture. Forbidden: business logic in UI or
  controllers when a service layer exists; direct storage access in handlers when a
  repository layer exists; bypassing existing services and abstractions without cause;
  circular module dependencies; dumping unrelated logic into catch-all files.
- If the architecture genuinely blocks the task, do not hack around it — propose a
  proper structural change and reflect it in the architecture docs once approved.
- A doc-comment-only boundary is not enforced. Use a type only the check can construct,
  or a gate no caller can skip — and test that it accepts, not only that it rejects.

## Temporary solutions

- Workarounds are allowed only exceptionally, and every one must be recorded
  explicitly: why it exists, where it lives, its limits and risks, and when it must be
  replaced.
- Hidden workarounds are forbidden. Do not scatter uncontrolled `TODO`/`FIXME` marks;
  important debt gets a task or an entry in the project's tracking process.

## Tech debt

- Debt found during a task that cannot be fixed now is recorded explicitly (in the
  final report at minimum), never disguised as a normal solution.
- Debt touching security, data integrity, performance, or stability is priority debt —
  call it out loudly.

# Security, Secrets, Dependencies, Portability

Purpose: nothing sensitive in the repo; every change safe within its area; the project
runs on any machine.

## Secrets — absolute ban

- NEVER put in code, git, tests, docs, or examples: passwords, API keys, tokens,
  private keys, real credentials, cookies, production `.env`, or personal user data.
- Secrets live only in `.env` (untracked), environment variables, secret managers, or
  CI/CD secrets. The repo may contain only a safe `.env.example`.
- A secret that ever reached git is compromised: rotate it; deleting the line in a new
  commit is not enough.

## Security in every task

Check within the area you touch: authorization and access rights, input validation,
injection, XSS and CSRF where applicable, unsafe redirects, file uploads, personal data
handling, public endpoints, token storage and transport, and access to admin functions.
Security is part of every task, not a future task.

## Dependencies

- No new dependency without justification: what for, can it be done without, is it
  maintained, known vulnerabilities, stack compatibility, does it duplicate an existing
  dependency, is it too heavy for the need.
- Never add a heavy library for one small function.
- After changing dependencies: update the lock file and verify the build.
- A new production dependency must be named in the final report.

## Portability

- No machine-specific values in code: local absolute paths, usernames, or anything
  environment-dependent. Such values go to configuration.
- The project must remain runnable by someone else using the project's documented tools.

# Quality: Tests, Errors, Data, Contracts, Performance

Purpose: changes are verified, honest about failure, and safe to release.

## Tests

- Cover new or changed code where reasonable: the happy path, validation errors, edge
  cases, access rights, service and storage behavior, and regressions for fixed bugs.
- NEVER delete, disable, or weaken tests just to make a build green.
- If tests were not added, say why in the final report.
- Prefer the project's designated check runner over ad-hoc command sequences, and keep
  that runner updated when a task adds an important new part of the system.

## Errors and logging

- Handle errors explicitly. Forbidden: silently swallowed errors, empty catch blocks,
  debug logs left after the task, secrets or personal data in logs, print-style
  debugging instead of real handling.
- Logs must say where it broke, which component, what context matters, and how critical
  it is. Useful, not noisy.

## Database migrations

- Schema changes happen ONLY through migrations.
- Never edit or rename an already-applied migration; never delete migrations without a
  separate decision; never make irreversible changes without risk analysis.
- Verify each migration on a clean database, on an existing database where applicable,
  and together with the code that uses the new structure.

## Contracts

- When a task changes an API or an artifact format, update the contract and generated
  types.
- Never silently change field names, data types, response structure, error codes,
  parameter requiredness, or endpoint behavior.
- Any breaking change must be named explicitly in the final report.

## Performance and releases

- No premature optimization, but no obviously wasteful patterns: N+1 queries, heavy
  per-request computation, render loops, unpaginated large reads, redundant calls,
  blocking operations in responsive paths.
- If a change may affect performance, say so in the final report.
- Every change should be revertible; for risky changes plan the rollback before merging.
- Large new features ship behind a feature flag where the project supports them;
  unfinished functionality must not be reachable by accident; stale flags get removed
  after stabilization.

# Multi-Assistant Collaboration

Purpose: several AI assistants and humans work in this repository across separate
sessions; git is the coordination surface and the rule modules are shared.

## Coordination through git

- Before non-trivial work, check
  `git log -10 --date=iso-strict --pretty=format:"%h %cd %s"` and
  `git status --short --branch`: recent commits may be another assistant's finished
  work — not yours to redo or second-guess.
- Never rewrite history on another assistant's in-flight branch. Build on top of it or
  ask first.
- Keep commits attributable: include the assistant identity trailer the project already
  uses (see recent `git log` for the convention).

## Shared rule modules

- All assistants obey the same rules from `.ai/universal/` and `.ai/project/`. There is
  exactly one source of truth.
- `CLAUDE.md` imports the modules natively; `AGENTS.md` is GENERATED from them. Never
  hand-edit `AGENTS.md`; edit the module and run the project's sync command (see the

- Re-read plans and rule files from disk instead of trusting memory of a previous
  session — files change between sessions.
- When context is shaky or the task is large, restate the task's acceptance criteria in
  the checklist before coding, and verify against files, not recollection.
- If two rules appear to conflict: the project module wins over the universal module;
  an explicit owner instruction in the current conversation wins over both. Say out
  loud which rule you chose and why.

# Rules Evolution: Keeping the Instructions Current

<!-- tier: extended -->

> **Essence.** Never weaken a rule to make a task easier — propose changes instead; autonomous edits may only clarify or correct, never loosen; every change needs a changelog entry and a regenerated entry point.

Purpose: the rule set is a living system, not a monument. It must absorb what agents
learn while working, stay factually true, and never silently rot. This module governs
how the rules change themselves.

## The prime safeguard

**Never weaken a rule to make your current task easier.** Editing the rules so that a
failing check passes, a forbidden action becomes allowed, or an inconvenient constraint
disappears is the single most damaging thing an agent can do here — it converts one bad
task into a permanent defect in every future task.

If a rule blocks you and you believe it is wrong, you do not edit it and proceed. You
stop, report the conflict, and propose the change for the owner. Finish the task under
the existing rule or leave it unfinished with an honest note.

## When you MUST propose a rule change

Proposing is mandatory, not optional, when any of these happen:

- **A rule is factually false.** A command, path, package, or file name in a module no
  longer matches reality.
- **You hit the same friction twice.** The same ambiguity or missing guidance cost you
  time in two separate tasks — that is a documentation defect, not bad luck.
- **A review keeps finding the same class of defect.** Repeated findings mean the rules
  failed to prevent them.
- **The owner gives an instruction that constrains future work.** Chat-only decisions
  are invisible to the next session; they must land in a module or in the decisions log.
- **The workflow changed.** A new stage, tool, gate, or command changed how work is
  actually done.
- **A rule proved harmful.** Following it produced a worse outcome than ignoring it
  would have.

## What you may change autonomously

Without asking, you may make the rules **more accurate** or **more clear**:

- correcting a stale path, command, package name, or file reference;
- fixing a contradiction between two modules by making them agree with the code;
- clarifying wording that misled you, without changing what is permitted;
- adding a concrete example of an existing rule;
- adding a genuinely new constraint the owner stated in the current conversation.

## What requires explicit owner approval

Ask, and wait, before you:

- remove a rule or make it optional;
- loosen a constraint, threshold, gate, or invariant;
- change the definition of done, the branch policy, or the publish policy;
- change anything in the project's invariants registry;
- change the language policy or the documentation policy;
- move a module between tiers in a way that drops content from the compiled entry point.

## How to change a module

1. Edit exactly one concern at a time in `.ai/universal/` or `.ai/project/`.
   Universal modules stay portable — no project names, paths, or stack specifics.
2. Add an entry to `.ai/CHANGELOG.md`: date, what changed, why, and who decided.
3. Regenerate the compiled entry point with the project's sync command.
4. If the change affects per-assistant workspaces, apply the mirrored edit on every
   side in the same task.
5. Commit the module, the changelog entry, and the regenerated entry point **together**.
   A module change without its regenerated entry point is a broken commit.

Never hand-edit the generated entry point. If it drifts, regenerate — do not patch.

## Review cadence

- **End of every task:** if the task surfaced friction, a stale fact, or a new
  constraint, fix the module now. Deferring is how rules rot.
- **End of every stage or milestone:** re-read the project modules against the code.
  Anything that no longer matches reality gets corrected or deleted.
- **On stage transition:** commands, layout, and gates usually change; the commands and
  project map modules almost always need an update.

## Retiring a rule

A rule that no longer applies is deleted, not left to confuse people. Deletion requires
owner approval, a changelog entry explaining why it is obsolete, and a check that no
other module still references it.

Superseded rules are removed, not commented out. Git history is the archive.

## Conflict resolution

When two rules disagree: the project module wins over the universal module; an explicit
owner instruction in the current conversation wins over both. Say out loud which rule
you followed and why — then, if the conflict is structural rather than one-off, fix it
in the modules so the next agent does not face the same ambiguity.

## Rule debt

Rule problems you notice but cannot fix in the current task are recorded like any other
debt: named in the final report, and, if significant, added to the decisions log as an
open question. Silently ignoring a known-wrong rule is a violation.

# Time and Timestamps: Never Take a Date Without Its Moment

> **Essence.** Read and report every date at full precision — hours, minutes, seconds, zone. For git use `--date=iso-strict` (`git log --pretty=format:"%h %cd %s"`); `--oneline`, `--date=short` and "2 days ago" never answer *when*.

Purpose: a date without a time cannot order two things that happened on the same day —
and on a project where several commits land in one day, that is precisely the question
being asked. Owner instruction, 2026-08-05.

## The rule

Whenever you take in information that carries a date — a commit, a file's mtime, a
history row, a log line, a release, a build, a database record — take the **full
moment** with it: hours, minutes, seconds, and the timezone (or an explicit note that
the value is UTC). Report it the same way.

Truncating is a decision, not a default. If a coarser rendering genuinely serves the
reader better in one specific place, say so at that place and explain why; never reach
for a day-granular helper because it is shorter.

Forbidden as an *answer* to "when did this happen":

- relative time alone — "2 days ago", "recently", "last week";
- a bare date — `2026-08-05` with no time;
- `git log --oneline`, which carries no time at all;
- a timestamp with no zone and no statement that it is UTC.

Relative time is fine as a *secondary* rendering next to the exact one — a tooltip, a
parenthetical. It is never the only thing shown.

## Git specifically

The commands to reach for, all read-only:

```powershell
git log -15 --date=iso-strict --pretty=format:"%h %cd %s"   # history, with committer dates
git show -s --format=fuller --date=iso-strict <ref>         # one commit, author AND committer
git log -1 --date=iso-strict --format=%cd -- <path>         # when a file last changed
```

`%cd` (committer date) is what orders history as it actually landed; `%ad` (author date)
survives a rebase or a cherry-pick unchanged, so the two disagree more often than people
expect. When the distinction could matter to the conclusion, read both and say which one
you are quoting.

`--date=iso-strict` gives `2026-08-05T14:23:07+03:00` — a real ISO 8601 instant with the
offset. Prefer it over `--date=iso` (a space instead of the `T`) and never fall back to
`--date=short` or `--date=relative`.

## In code and artifacts

- A timestamp written into an artifact, a log line, a database row, or an interface
  carries seconds. A formatting helper that drops the time of day does not belong in a
  shared utility module: without one available, truncation has to be written out
  deliberately at the call site, where a reviewer can see it.
- Store the full instant (epoch seconds, or better) even when the current display is
  coarser. Precision that was never captured cannot be recovered later.
- State the zone. If everything renders UTC, say `UTC` in the rendered string rather
  than leaving a reader to guess at their own offset.

# Claude Code Project Configuration

Project-scoped Claude Code configuration for ChatImport. Claude Code is the priority
assistant; Codex and Gemini CLI read the same rules through `AGENTS.md`.

Durable rules live in the shared modules under `.ai/` (universal + project). `CLAUDE.md`
imports them natively via `@` syntax. Subagents should read `AGENTS.md` — the compiled
single-file ruleset.

## Files

- `settings.json` — allowlist for routine read and verification commands; denylist for
  destructive git operations and for reading `.env` and session files.
- `agents/` — project subagents; the **source** of the generated `.codex/agents/`.
- `skills/` — reusable workflows; the **source** of the generated `.codex/skills/`.
- `settings.local.json` — personal overrides, ignored by git.

After editing an agent or a skill, run `just agents` and commit the regenerated `.codex/`.

## Recommended delegation

Do task-owning work on the main thread; spawn a subagent only for independent work that
does not need the main thread's full context:

# Fixing a Failing Check

1. Reproduce with `just check`; CI runs the same sections as separate jobs (see
   `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), plus gitleaks.
2. Run the failing section alone: `just lint`, `just typecheck`, `just test`,
   `just agents-check`, `just language`, `uv lock --check`.
3. Typical causes:
   - `agents-check`: `.ai/` or `.claude/agents|skills` changed without regeneration. Run
     `just agents` and commit the generated files.
   - `language`: Cyrillic in a tracked file. Translate it; only genuine data belongs in
     the allowed paths of `scripts/check_language.py`.
   - `uv lock --check`: `pyproject.toml` changed without `uv lock`.
   - pyright strict: an untyped library value leaking out — type it at the boundary.
   - Windows-only failures: see the platform notes in `.ai/project/14-command-reference.md`.
   - gitleaks: a secret reached git. Remove it **and rotate it**; deleting the line is not
     enough.
4. Never delete, skip or loosen a test or a check to get green, and never use
   `--no-verify`. If a rule itself is wrong, follow the `rules-evolution` skill.

# Reviewing Changes

Run this **before** merging and before the final report.

```bash
git status --short --branch
git diff chatimport...HEAD
```

For an independent pass, delegate to the `chatimport-quality-reviewer` agent; for anything
touching sessions, secrets or personal data, also to `chatimport-privacy-security`.

## Mandatory checklist

1. **Scope.** No changes the task did not require.
2. **Boundaries.** Telethon only in `telegram/`; mapper, storage and trim free of client,
   CLI and tray; no logic in commands or menus.
3. **One writer.** Only the chat worker (or the trimmer under the chat lock) writes data.
4. **Data.** Record and `state.json` changes keep old files readable (`v` bumped when
   meaning changes); history appended, never rewritten; `msg_id` order inside parts.
5. **Crash safety.** Atomic writes where required; no file left open between writes;
   dedup by `last_id` keeps restarts free of duplicates.
6. **Privacy.** No secrets, sessions, real config or message text in code, fixtures or
   logs; nothing leaves the machine.
7. **Time.** UTC-aware datetimes only.
8. **Language.** English only outside the allowed data paths (`just language`).
9. **Tests.** Not deleted or weakened; Telegram not called; regressions covered.
10. **Documents.** Project map, architecture, roadmap status, decisions, README,
    changelogs, rule sync as needed (`just agents-check`).
11. **Leftovers.** Debug output, temp files, commented-out code.

Fix serious findings in the same task; record unrelated problems separately. If there are
no findings, say so plainly.

---
name: format-change
description: Use when changing a persistent format — the JSONL record, file and folder naming, state.json, _status.json, the control-command files, config.toml or chats.toml — keeping existing data and configuration loading.
---

# Changing a Persistent Format

ChatImport's files outlive the code that wrote them. Every change keeps what is already on
the owner's disk readable.

## JSONL records

1. A new field is optional for old records and keeps `v`. Removing a field or changing its
   meaning bumps `v`, and readers accept every `v` ever written.
2. Never rewrite existing parts to migrate them; history is append-only.
3. Update `docs/architecture.md` §6 and the mapper's table-driven tests.

## File and folder naming

Part names (`YYYY-MM_NNN.jsonl`) and folder discovery by `state.json` must keep finding
existing folders. A rename rule applies to new files only.

## `state.json`, `_status.json`, control files

`state.json` is a cache rebuilt from the files: a new key has a default and recover fills
it. `_status.json` and control files are read by other processes — add fields, do not
rename them without a `v` bump on both sides.

## `config.toml` and `chats.toml`

A new setting has a safe default (an empty file still works), appears in
`config.example.toml` / `chats.example.toml` and `.ai/project/14-command-reference.md`,
and has a test. A broken library file never stops the service: it keeps the last valid
version. Renaming a key keeps the old one working for one release or is called out as a
breaking change.

## Finish

`just check`, then name any breaking change in the final report and `CHANGELOG.md`.

# Repository Maintenance

## Fast paths

```bash
just check          # the gate (CI runs the same sections)
just agents         # AGENTS.md + .codex mirror from .ai/ and .claude/
just doctor         # read-only toolchain check
just hooks          # every pre-commit hook over the repository
```

## Rules

- Generated, never hand-edited: `AGENTS.md`, `.codex/agents/*`, `.codex/skills/*`. Edit the
  source, regenerate, commit both together.
- The `AGENTS.md` budget is 30 KiB: tighten a module, or mark a situational one
  `<!-- tier: extended -->` with an `> **Essence.**` line (moving tiers needs owner approval).
- Rule changes follow the `rules-evolution` skill, including `.ai/CHANGELOG.md`.
- `.claude/settings.json`: extending the allowlist is fine; removing a deny entry needs
  explicit owner approval.
- Version lives in `pyproject.toml` (SemVer); a release is a `vX.Y.Z` tag plus a
  `CHANGELOG.md` section.
- Dependencies through `uv add`; a new production dependency is justified and named in the
  final report. Dependabot reads only `main`; update this branch by hand with `uv lock --upgrade-package`.

## State documents

Step done → `docs/ROADMAP.md` `**Status.**` line. Shape changed → project map and
`docs/architecture.md`. Owner decision → `docs/decisions.md`. Architecture decision →
`docs/adr/`. Task closed → `task-checklist.md` with honest `+`/`-` marks.

## Publishing

No pull requests. Merge the task branch into `chatimport` with `git merge --ff-only` after
a green gate and push `chatimport` — only when the owner asked in the current task. `main`
(ChatRadar) is not touched from this line of work.

---

# Evolving the Agent Rules

The full protocol is `.ai/universal/08-rules-evolution.md`; this is the operational path.

## The prime safeguard

**Never weaken a rule to make your current task easier.** If a rule blocks you and you
believe it is wrong, stop, report the conflict, and propose the change.

## 1. Is a change required?

Mandatory when a rule is factually false, the same friction cost time twice, reviews keep
finding the same defect, the owner gave a standing instruction, the workflow changed, or a
rule proved harmful.

## 2. May you do it alone?

**Autonomous:** fixing a stale path or command, resolving a contradiction against the code,
clarifying wording, adding an example, recording a constraint the owner just stated.

**Owner approval:** removing or loosening a rule, gate or guardrail; changing the definition
of done, the publish policy, the language policy or the documentation policy.

## 3. Apply

1. Edit exactly one concern in `.ai/universal/` (portable, no project specifics) or
   `.ai/project/`; for agents and skills edit `.claude/`.
2. Add an entry to `.ai/CHANGELOG.md`: date, what, why, who decided.
3. Run `just agents`, then `just agents-check`.
4. Commit the module, the changelog entry and the regenerated files together.

## Retiring a rule

Delete it (git history is the archive) with owner approval, a changelog entry, and a check
that nothing else references it.

# Executing a Roadmap Stage

One `docs/ROADMAP.md` stage is one task. Do not merge two stages into one task, and do not
skip the order without an owner decision recorded in `docs/decisions.md`.

## 1. Orientation (mandatory, no skipping)

```bash
git status --short --branch
git log -15 --date=iso-strict --pretty=format:"%h %cd %s"
```

Then read, in order: `docs/ROADMAP.md` (the first stage without a `**Status.**` line is
yours), `task-checklist.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, and the matching sections of
`docs/architecture.md`. Product intent: `docs/vision.md`.

If `task-checklist.md` still has open `[ ]` items from a previous session, resolve them
first.

## 2. Planning

For a large or unfamiliar stage, delegate to the `chatimport-step-planner` subagent.
Define boundaries, the owning module for each piece, every data format touched, risks and
acceptance criteria. Fill `task-checklist.md` with `[ ]` items grouped into preparation /
implementation / verification / completion, and **commit it before writing code**.

## 3. Branch

This line of work lives on `chatimport`, not `main`:

```bash
git checkout chatimport
git pull --ff-only origin chatimport
git checkout -b feat/stage-0-N-short-description
```

## 4. Implementation

Delegate where it helps: `chatimport-telegram`, `chatimport-storage`,
`chatimport-interfaces`, `chatimport-platform`. Format changes follow `format-change`.

## 5. Verification

```bash
just check
```

Exercise the acceptance criteria end to end where possible (`chatimport` commands with
`CHATIMPORT_ROOT` pointing at a temporary folder and the fake Telegram client). A live
Telegram run is the owner's step unless they ask otherwise. Run the `code-review` skill or
the `chatimport-quality-reviewer` subagent before finalizing.

## 6. Completion

- Mark checklist items `+`/`-` honestly.
- Add the `**Status.**` line under the stage in `docs/ROADMAP.md` and update its table row.
- Update `.ai/project/10-project-map.md`, `.ai/project/14-command-reference.md`,
  `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` where the change is visible there.
- If the stage exposed stale or missing rules, apply the `rules-evolution` skill.
- Fast-forward merge into `chatimport` only with a green gate; push only when the owner
  asked.
- Write the final report in Russian: what was done, what was verified, what was not done.

# GENERATED from .claude/skills/ci-fix/SKILL.md by just agents - do not edit.

# Fixing a Failing Check

1. Reproduce with `just check`; CI runs the same sections as separate jobs (see
   `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), plus gitleaks.
2. Run the failing section alone: `just lint`, `just typecheck`, `just test`,
   `just agents-check`, `just language`, `uv lock --check`.
3. Typical causes:
   - `agents-check`: `.ai/` or `.claude/agents|skills` changed without regeneration. Run
     `just agents` and commit the generated files.
   - `language`: Cyrillic in a tracked file. Translate it; only genuine data belongs in
     the allowed paths of `scripts/check_language.py`.
   - `uv lock --check`: `pyproject.toml` changed without `uv lock`.
   - pyright strict: an untyped library value leaking out — type it at the boundary.
   - Windows-only failures: see the platform notes in `.ai/project/14-command-reference.md`.
   - gitleaks: a secret reached git. Remove it **and rotate it**; deleting the line is not
     enough.
4. Never delete, skip or loosen a test or a check to get green, and never use
   `--no-verify`. If a rule itself is wrong, follow the `rules-evolution` skill.

# Reviewing Changes

Run this **before** merging and before the final report.

```bash
git status --short --branch
git diff chatimport...HEAD
```

For an independent pass, delegate to the `chatimport-quality-reviewer` agent; for anything
touching sessions, secrets or personal data, also to `chatimport-privacy-security`.

## Mandatory checklist

1. **Scope.** No changes the task did not require.
2. **Boundaries.** Telethon only in `telegram/`; mapper, storage and trim free of client,
   CLI and tray; no logic in commands or menus.
3. **One writer.** Only the chat worker (or the trimmer under the chat lock) writes data.
4. **Data.** Record and `state.json` changes keep old files readable (`v` bumped when
   meaning changes); history appended, never rewritten; `msg_id` order inside parts.
5. **Crash safety.** Atomic writes where required; no file left open between writes;
   dedup by `last_id` keeps restarts free of duplicates.
6. **Privacy.** No secrets, sessions, real config or message text in code, fixtures or
   logs; nothing leaves the machine.
7. **Time.** UTC-aware datetimes only.
8. **Language.** English only outside the allowed data paths (`just language`).
9. **Tests.** Not deleted or weakened; Telegram not called; regressions covered.
10. **Documents.** Project map, architecture, roadmap status, decisions, README,
    changelogs, rule sync as needed (`just agents-check`).
11. **Leftovers.** Debug output, temp files, commented-out code.

no findings, say so plainly.

# GENERATED from .claude/skills/format-change/SKILL.md by just agents - do not edit.

description: Use when changing a persistent format — the JSONL record, file and folder naming, state.json, _status.json, the control-command files, config.toml or chats.toml — keeping existing data and configuration loading.
---

# Changing a Persistent Format

ChatImport's files outlive the code that wrote them. Every change keeps what is already on
the owner's disk readable.

## JSONL records

1. A new field is optional for old records and keeps `v`. Removing a field or changing its
   meaning bumps `v`, and readers accept every `v` ever written.
2. Never rewrite existing parts to migrate them; history is append-only.
3. Update `docs/architecture.md` §6 and the mapper's table-driven tests.

## File and folder naming

Part names (`YYYY-MM_NNN.jsonl`) and folder discovery by `state.json` must keep finding
existing folders. A rename rule applies to new files only.

## `state.json`, `_status.json`, control files

`state.json` is a cache rebuilt from the files: a new key has a default and recover fills
it. `_status.json` and control files are read by other processes — add fields, do not
rename them without a `v` bump on both sides.

## `config.toml` and `chats.toml`

A new setting has a safe default (an empty file still works), appears in
`config.example.toml` / `chats.example.toml` and `.ai/project/14-command-reference.md`,
and has a test. A broken library file never stops the service: it keeps the last valid
version. Renaming a key keeps the old one working for one release or is called out as a
breaking change.

## Finish

`just check`, then name any breaking change in the final report and `CHANGELOG.md`.

# Repository Maintenance

## Fast paths

```bash
just check          # the gate (CI runs the same sections)
just agents         # AGENTS.md + .codex mirror from .ai/ and .claude/
just doctor         # read-only toolchain check
just hooks          # every pre-commit hook over the repository
```

## Rules

- Generated, never hand-edited: `AGENTS.md`, `.codex/agents/*`, `.codex/skills/*`. Edit the
  source, regenerate, commit both together.
- The `AGENTS.md` budget is 30 KiB: tighten a module, or mark a situational one
  `<!-- tier: extended -->` with an `> **Essence.**` line (moving tiers needs owner approval).
- Rule changes follow the `rules-evolution` skill, including `.ai/CHANGELOG.md`.
- `.claude/settings.json`: extending the allowlist is fine; removing a deny entry needs
  explicit owner approval.
- Version lives in `pyproject.toml` (SemVer); a release is a `vX.Y.Z` tag plus a
  `CHANGELOG.md` section.
- Dependencies through `uv add`; a new production dependency is justified and named in the
  final report. Dependabot reads only `main`; update this branch by hand with `uv lock --upgrade-package`.

## State documents

Step done → `docs/ROADMAP.md` `**Status.**` line. Shape changed → project map and
`docs/architecture.md`. Owner decision → `docs/decisions.md`. Architecture decision →
`docs/adr/`. Task closed → `task-checklist.md` with honest `+`/`-` marks.

## Publishing

No pull requests. Merge the task branch into `chatimport` with `git merge --ff-only` after
a green gate and push `chatimport` — only when the owner asked in the current task. `main`
(ChatRadar) is not touched from this line of work.

description: Use when the agent rules need to change — a rule is stale, wrong, missing, or the owner gave a new standing instruction. Covers what may change autonomously, what needs approval, and the sync procedure.
---

# Evolving the Agent Rules

The full protocol is `.ai/universal/08-rules-evolution.md`; this is the operational path.

## The prime safeguard

**Never weaken a rule to make your current task easier.** If a rule blocks you and you
believe it is wrong, stop, report the conflict, and propose the change.

## 1. Is a change required?

Mandatory when a rule is factually false, the same friction cost time twice, reviews keep
finding the same defect, the owner gave a standing instruction, the workflow changed, or a
rule proved harmful.

## 2. May you do it alone?

**Autonomous:** fixing a stale path or command, resolving a contradiction against the code,
clarifying wording, adding an example, recording a constraint the owner just stated.

**Owner approval:** removing or loosening a rule, gate or guardrail; changing the definition
of done, the publish policy, the language policy or the documentation policy.

## 3. Apply

1. Edit exactly one concern in `.ai/universal/` (portable, no project specifics) or
   `.ai/project/`; for agents and skills edit `.claude/`.
2. Add an entry to `.ai/CHANGELOG.md`: date, what, why, who decided.
3. Run `just agents`, then `just agents-check`.
4. Commit the module, the changelog entry and the regenerated files together.

## Retiring a rule

Delete it (git history is the archive) with owner approval, a changelog entry, and a check
that nothing else references it.

# Executing a Roadmap Stage

One `docs/ROADMAP.md` stage is one task. Do not merge two stages into one task, and do not
skip the order without an owner decision recorded in `docs/decisions.md`.

## 1. Orientation (mandatory, no skipping)

```bash
git status --short --branch
git log -15 --date=iso-strict --pretty=format:"%h %cd %s"
```

Then read, in order: `docs/ROADMAP.md` (the first stage without a `**Status.**` line is
yours), `task-checklist.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, and the matching sections of
`docs/architecture.md`. Product intent: `docs/vision.md`.

If `task-checklist.md` still has open `[ ]` items from a previous session, resolve them
first.

## 2. Planning

For a large or unfamiliar stage, delegate to the `chatimport-step-planner` subagent.
Define boundaries, the owning module for each piece, every data format touched, risks and
acceptance criteria. Fill `task-checklist.md` with `[ ]` items grouped into preparation /
implementation / verification / completion, and **commit it before writing code**.

## 3. Branch

This line of work lives on `chatimport`, not `main`:

```bash
git checkout chatimport
git pull --ff-only origin chatimport
git checkout -b feat/stage-0-N-short-description
```

## 4. Implementation

Delegate where it helps: `chatimport-telegram`, `chatimport-storage`,
`chatimport-interfaces`, `chatimport-platform`. Format changes follow `format-change`.

## 5. Verification

```bash
just check
```

Exercise the acceptance criteria end to end where possible (`chatimport` commands with
`CHATIMPORT_ROOT` pointing at a temporary folder and the fake Telegram client). A live
Telegram run is the owner's step unless they ask otherwise. Run the `code-review` skill or
the `chatimport-quality-reviewer` subagent before finalizing.

## 6. Completion

- Mark checklist items `+`/`-` honestly.
- Add the `**Status.**` line under the stage in `docs/ROADMAP.md` and update its table row.
- Update `.ai/project/10-project-map.md`, `.ai/project/14-command-reference.md`,
  `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` where the change is visible there.
- If the stage exposed stale or missing rules, apply the `rules-evolution` skill.
- Fast-forward merge into `chatimport` only with a green gate; push only when the owner
  asked.
- Write the final report in Russian: what was done, what was verified, what was not done.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, chatimport]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

env:
  UV_FROZEN: "1"
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true
      - name: Lock file is up to date
        run: uv lock --check
      - name: ruff check
        run: uv run ruff check --output-format=github .
      - name: ruff format
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

  typecheck:
    name: Typecheck (pyright strict)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true
      - run: uv sync
      - run: uv run pyright

  test:
    name: Tests (${{ matrix.os }}, py${{ matrix.python }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
        python: ["3.14"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      - name: Qt system libraries
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libegl1 libgl1 libxkbcommon0 libdbus-1-3 libfontconfig1 libglib2.0-0
      - run: uv sync
      - name: pytest
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          uv run pytest --cov --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=xml 2>&1 | tee pytest.log
      - name: Show test failures as annotations
        if: failure()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          grep -E "^(FAILED|ERROR)|^E  " pytest.log | head -40 | cut -c1-400 | while IFS= read -r line; do echo "::error::${line}"; done
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        with:
          name: coverage
          path: coverage.xml
          retention-days: 7

  assistants:
    name: Assistant rules and language
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true
      - name: AGENTS.md and .codex in sync with .ai/ and .claude/
        run: uv run python scripts/sync_agents.py --check
      - name: English only
        run: uv run python scripts/check_language.py

  secrets:
    name: Secret scan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v2
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: <REDACTED> secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# ChatImport - working notes for Codex and other AI assistants

This file is the entry point for Codex and any tool that reads AGENTS.md. It is assembled
from the shared rule modules in `.ai/`, so every assistant follows identical rules. Later
sections override earlier ones; an explicit owner instruction in the current conversation
overrides everything. Start every task with the orientation ritual in the progress module.

<!-- module: .ai/universal/01-workflow.md -->

# Workflow: Git, Branches, Commits

Purpose: every task follows one predictable git cycle. No exceptions without an
explicit owner instruction in the current conversation.

## Branch discipline

- NEVER develop directly on `main`.
- Start every task from up-to-date `main`:
  `git checkout main` → `git pull --ff-only origin main` → `git checkout -b <branch>`.
- Branch name format: `type/short-task-description`
  (types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, `docs`, `ci`, `perf`, `security`).
- Uninformative branch names (`test`, `fix`, `work`, `final`, `new`) are forbidden.
- Merge into `main` only fast-forward (`git merge --ff-only`) and only after the
  project's full quality gate is green.
- Push to `origin/main` only when the owner explicitly asked for a publish within the
  current task. Work-in-progress branch pushes are allowed (for example, to publish
  the task checklist before starting work).
- Delete the task branch after it is merged.

## Commits

- Message format: `type: short description of what and why`.
- One commit = one logically complete unit. Do not mix a bug fix, a refactor,
  formatting, and new features in a single commit unless they are one inseparable task.
- Forbidden messages: `fix`, `update`, `wip`, `changes`, `final`, `123`.
- Keep commits attributable: include the assistant identity trailer the project already
  uses (check a recent `git log` for the convention).

## Quality gate before merge

- Run the project's checks (see the project commands module) before merging.
- If mandatory checks fail, merging into `main` is forbidden until fixed or the owner
  explicitly decides otherwise.
- Before merging, self-review the diff: changes match the task, no stray files, no
  debug leftovers, no secrets, no accidental unrelated edits.

When unsure whether an action counts as "explicitly requested": ask, or stop after the
branch commit and report instead of pushing.

<!-- module: .ai/universal/02-task-checklist.md -->

# Task Checklist and Definition of Done

Purpose: every task is planned before it starts and honestly accounted for after it
ends, in a file any reviewer can read without the conversation.

## task-checklist.md protocol

A file named `task-checklist.md` lives in the repository root and is always tracked by
git (never in `.gitignore`).

Before starting a task:

1. Clear or recreate `task-checklist.md` for the new task.
2. Write the main stages, checks, and expected outcomes as `[ ]` items, grouped into
   short sections (preparation / implementation / verification / completion).
   Moderate detail — stages, not keystrokes.
3. Commit the checklist BEFORE doing the main work.

After finishing the task:

4. Mark every item: `+` done, `-` not done or partially done.
5. Commit the filled checklist together with the completed work.
6. Never hide unfinished items — a `-` with an honest note is correct; a silently
   ignored item is a violation.

## Definition of Done

A task is complete only when ALL of the following hold:

- code written and matching the task, without unrequested scope;
- code formatted; lint and type checks pass;
- tests added or updated where reasonable; existing tests pass;
- project builds; no obvious errors in logs;
- no secrets, no temp files, no accidental changes in unrelated files;
- architecture and state docs updated if the task changed the system's shape;
- task checklist filled with `+`/`-`;
- final report written.

## Final report

The final report is ALWAYS the last step of a task. It states: what was done; which
files and areas changed; which checks ran and their results; dependency, API, database,
or config changes; security, performance, and compatibility risks; and — explicitly and
honestly — anything that was not done or failed.

---

<!-- module: .ai/universal/03-scope-and-code-style.md -->

# Scope Control and Code Style

Purpose: change only what the task requires, and keep code readable without decoration.

## Minimal changes

- Touch only what the current task needs. Forbidden without necessity:
  mass-reformatting other files, renaming things outside the task, changing
  architecture "while at it", rewriting working code without cause, changing UI when
  the task is not about the interface, deleting existing functionality without a
  direct requirement.
- If you discover an unrelated problem, record it separately (report it, or file it per
  the project's process) — do not mix it into the current diff.
- Do not create new documentation (README, `.md`, `.txt`) unless the task requires it
  directly. Exception: the project's designated architecture and progress documents,
  which must be kept current.

## Comments

- No comments by default. Code must be clear through structure and naming.
- A comment is allowed only when the task demands it, or when important logic stays
  non-obvious even with good naming. It explains the non-obvious "why", never restates
  the code.
- Stale, false, or misleading comments are forbidden. No doc comments that merely
  repeat a function name.

## File size

- Regular code files: keep under roughly 1000 lines; split by meaning when approaching
  the limit. Projects may set a stricter limit — the stricter limit wins.
- Application entry points (`main`-type files): under roughly 100 lines; extract
  configuration, startup, and service initialization into modules.
- Exemptions: test files, developer-tool scripts, and any files the project explicitly
  exempts.

## Frontend restraint

- No visual polish (styling, animations, decorative elements, redesign) unless the task
  is explicitly about appearance.
- When a task needs an interface, build the minimum that exercises the business logic
  correctly.
- Never change visual style, interface structure, component behavior, or user flows
  without a direct requirement.

---

<!-- module: .ai/universal/04-architecture-boundaries.md -->

# Architecture Boundaries, Workarounds, Tech Debt

Purpose: respect the project's layering; make every shortcut visible.

## Boundaries

- Follow the project's existing architecture. Forbidden: business logic in UI or
  controllers when a service layer exists; direct storage access in handlers when a
  repository layer exists; bypassing existing services and abstractions without cause;
  circular module dependencies; dumping unrelated logic into catch-all files.
- If the architecture genuinely blocks the task, do not hack around it — propose a
  proper structural change and reflect it in the architecture docs once approved.
- A doc-comment-only boundary is not enforced. Use a type only the check can construct,
  or a gate no caller can skip — and test that it accepts, not only that it rejects.

## Temporary solutions

- Workarounds are allowed only exceptionally, and every one must be recorded
  explicitly: why it exists, where it lives, its limits and risks, and when it must be
  replaced.
- Hidden workarounds are forbidden. Do not scatter uncontrolled `TODO`/`FIXME` marks;
  important debt gets a task or an entry in the project's tracking process.

## Tech debt

- Debt found during a task that cannot be fixed now is recorded explicitly (in the
  final report at minimum), never disguised as a normal solution.
- Debt touching security, data integrity, performance, or stability is priority debt —
  call it out loudly.

---

<!-- module: .ai/universal/05-security-and-secrets.md -->

# Security, Secrets, Dependencies, Portability

Purpose: nothing sensitive in the repo; every change safe within its area; the project
runs on any machine.

## Secrets — absolute ban

- NEVER put in code, git, tests, docs, or examples: passwords, API keys, tokens,
  private keys, real credentials, cookies, production `.env`, or personal user data.
- Secrets live only in `.env` (untracked), environment variables, secret managers, or
  CI/CD secrets. The repo may contain only a safe `.env.example`.
- A secret that ever reached git is compromised: rotate it; deleting the line in a new
  commit is not enough.

## Security in every task

Check within the area you touch: authorization and access rights, input validation,
injection, XSS and CSRF where applicable, unsafe redirects, file uploads, personal data
handling, public endpoints, token storage and transport, and access to admin functions.
Security is part of every task, not a future task.

## Dependencies

- No new dependency without justification: what for, can it be done without, is it
  maintained, known vulnerabilities, stack compatibility, does it duplicate an existing
  dependency, is it too heavy for the need.
- Never add a heavy library for one small function.
- After changing dependencies: update the lock file and verify the build.
- A new production dependency must be named in the final report.

## Portability

- No machine-specific values in code: local absolute paths, usernames, or anything
  environment-dependent. Such values go to configuration.
- The project must remain runnable by someone else using the project's documented tools.

---

<!-- module: .ai/universal/06-quality-and-testing.md -->

# Quality: Tests, Errors, Data, Contracts, Performance

Purpose: changes are verified, honest about failure, and safe to release.

## Tests

- Cover new or changed code where reasonable: the happy path, validation errors, edge
  cases, access rights, service and storage behavior, and regressions for fixed bugs.
- NEVER delete, disable, or weaken tests just to make a build green.
- If tests were not added, say why in the final report.
- Prefer the project's designated check runner over ad-hoc command sequences, and keep
  that runner updated when a task adds an important new part of the system.

## Errors and logging

- Handle errors explicitly. Forbidden: silently swallowed errors, empty catch blocks,
  debug logs left after the task, secrets or personal data in logs, print-style
  debugging instead of real handling.
- Logs must say where it broke, which component, what context matters, and how critical
  it is. Useful, not noisy.

## Database migrations

- Schema changes happen ONLY through migrations.
- Never edit or rename an already-applied migration; never delete migrations without a
  separate decision; never make irreversible changes without risk analysis.
- Verify each migration on a clean database, on an existing database where applicable,
  and together with the code that uses the new structure.

## Contracts

- When a task changes an API or an artifact format, update the contract and generated
  types.
- Never silently change field names, data types, response structure, error codes,
  parameter requiredness, or endpoint behavior.
- Any breaking change must be named explicitly in the final report.

## Performance and releases

- No premature optimization, but no obviously wasteful patterns: N+1 queries, heavy
  per-request computation, render loops, unpaginated large reads, redundant calls,
  blocking operations in responsive paths.
- If a change may affect performance, say so in the final report.
- Every change should be revertible; for risky changes plan the rollback before merging.
- Large new features ship behind a feature flag where the project supports them;
  unfinished functionality must not be reachable by accident; stale flags get removed
  after stabilization.
